title: Tamil Nadu Politics – Evening Brief – 7 November 2026
headline: Tamil Nadu Political Landscape Shaken as TVK Government Allocates ₹2,000 Crore for Student Laptops, Scraps Kurian Panel, and Confronts Opposition Over Controversial 'AI Book Scandal'

sections.big_picture:
The Tamil Nadu political arena witnessed high-stakes policy shifts and intense partisan confrontations as Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's administration rolled out major fiscal commitments alongside sweeping administrative retrenchments. The government sanctioned a robust ₹2,000 crore allocation for the Vetri Laptop Scheme aimed at bolstering digital education for college students, signaling a direct welfare-oriented push. Concurrently, the administration dissolved the High-Level Committee on Union-State Relations, previously headed by retired Supreme Court Justice Kurian Joseph, arguing that its mandate overlapped with the newly reconstituted Tamil Nadu State Law Commission.

These administrative actions triggered immediate, sharp pushback from major opposition parties. The DMK launched a multi-front counter-offensive, filing formal complaints with the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) over alleged large-scale procurement irregularities—dubbed the 'AI book scam'—at Coimbatore's Periyar Arivulagam library. Prominent literary figures and ruling party ministers alike flagged inflated pricing and suspected artificial intelligence-generated errors across thousands of procured volumes. Meanwhile, Chief Minister Vijay escalated inter-state tensions by formally writing to Prime Minister Narendra Modi to register vehement opposition against central inspection teams visiting the disputed Mekedatu dam site, setting the stage for protracted legislative and legal battles across the state.

sections.government_and_administration: - **TVK Administration Discontinues Justice Kurian Joseph Panel, Citing Statutory Overlap with Law Commission:** In an official government order dated November 6, Public Secretary E. Sundaravalli announced the immediate discontinuation of the High-Level Committee on Union-State Relations, headed by retired Supreme Court judge Justice Kurian Joseph. Originally constituted by the previous DMK government on April 17, 2025, the panel was actively drafting the second segment of its comprehensive report scheduled for release by May 31, 2027. The state government justified the scrapping by stating that the mandate of the Kurian committee had become entirely redundant following the reconstitution of the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission on August 7, 2026, which now possesses an expanded jurisdiction to examine inter-state and Centre-state administrative dynamics. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/tvk-govt-scraps-justice-kurian-joseph-panel-on-union-state-relations))
sections.political_parties_and_opposition: - **DMK and AIADMK Lead Fierce Condemnations Against TVK Regime Over Scrapped Panels and Governance Stunts:** DMK President M.K. Stalin issued a scathing condemnation against the ruling TVK administration for abruptly canceling the high-level committee on Centre-state relations established during the DMK tenure, accusing the ruling party of political vindictiveness and undermining federal accountability. Concurrently, AIADMK General Secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami targeted Chief Minister Vijay over the Periyar Arivulagam library book controversy, remarking sarcastically whether orchestrating high-profile library openings akin to cinematic productions suffices as governance. Opposition parties have vowed to escalate protests inside and outside the legislative assembly, demanding white papers on recent administrative cancellations and transparent accountability regarding public expenditure on disputed procurements. ([DinaMani](https://news.google.?oc=5))
sections.assembly_courts_and_policy: - **Madras High Court Rules Statutory Force of Ban on Engaging Children in Electoral Campaigns:** Justice K. Kumaresh Babu of the Madras High Court delivered a significant judicial ruling on Thursday, affirming that the statutory prohibition against utilizing children in political campaign work carries absolute legal force and binding enforceability. The observation was made while presiding over an election petition filed by DMK candidate Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi, who challenged the election victory of TVK MLA Vijayakumar alias Navalpattu Viji from the Thiruverumbur assembly constituency during the fiercely contested 2026 general elections. The court emphasized that political parties flouting election commission guidelines regarding minor participation face severe statutory penalties, setting a strict precedent for future electoral litigation and campaign monitoring across the state. ([The Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/chennai/ban-on-using-kids-in-poll-work-has-statutory-force-rules-madras-high-court/articleshow/135638649.cms))
sections.district_developments: - **Coimbatore Administrative Machinery Mobilized Following Literary and Political Fallout at Periyar Library:** District administrative authorities in Coimbatore faced intense local scrutiny following revelations of severe cataloging inaccuracies, inflated pricing, and suspected artificial intelligence-generated texts discovered among 1,800 newly procured books at the recently inaugurated Periyar Arivulagam library. Prominent literary figures, led by writer Perumal Murugan, documented misleading historical descriptions and distorted biographies of prominent Tamil leaders during site inspections. Local civic activists and opposition party cadres staged demonstration rallies outside district administrative headquarters, demanding an exhaustive audit of municipal and district-level library acquisitions. In response, district education officials have sequestered the contested volumes pending a forensic audit ordered by the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption. ([The Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/chennai/errors-in-1800-books-at-tamil-nadu-library-writer-flags-possible-ai-use-questions-authorship/articleshow/135629171.cms))
sections.what_to_watch_next: Over the next 24 to 48 hours, political observers will closely monitor developments surrounding the formal DVAC probe into the Periyar Arivulagam library book scandal and potential legal filings by opposition parties in the Madras High Court. Attention will also focus on responses from the Union Ministry of Water Resources regarding Chief Minister Vijay's letter opposing the Mekedatu dam site inspections, alongside scheduled legislative committee meetings reviewing the implementation timeline and procurement transparency parameters for the newly announced ₹2,000-crore Vetri Laptop Scheme.
